speaker: Doctor
text: I see you are experiencing progressive difficulty walking, urinary incontinence, and speech difficulties. To begin our assessment, have you noticed any limb weakness, numbness, or balance problems in the past few months?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old male. The patient has been experiencing a gradual difficulty in walking over the past 3 months, requiring wheelchair assistance for the last month. Additionally, there is a history of urinary incontinence for 1 year and recent onset of speech slurring making communication challenging.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The clinical picture of progressive gait disturbance, urinary incontinence, and dysarthria suggests involvement of the cervical spinal cord. Can you tell me if you have experienced any specific pain in your neck or back, or if you feel like your legs are crossing over each other when walking (scissor gait)?

REQUEST TEST: MRI Cervical Spine
REQUEST IMAGES: Cervical_Spine_MRI

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Cervical Spondylotic Myelopathy (CSPM)

The MRI and clinical history confirm spinal cord compression at the cervical level causing progressive myelopathy. The presence of bladder dysfunction and dysarthria alongside gait disturbance in a 54-year-old male strongly points to this degenerative condition affecting the cervical spine.
